insight.title: Classic SIRS Presentation
insight.body: Fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypotension with altered mental status strongly suggest sepsis. Two or more SIRS criteria with suspected infection should trigger the sepsis pathway immediately.

insight.title: Subtle Sepsis Clues
insight.body: Sepsis may present with only low-grade fever and vague weakness. A recent pneumonia with tachypnea and borderline hypotension should raise suspicion even when the patient appears alert.

insight.title: Hypothermic Sepsis
insight.body: Septic patients may present with hypothermia instead of fever — especially elderly and nursing home residents. A temperature below 96.8°F with hypotension and AMS is sepsis until proven otherwise.
